theorem_title: Lemma 2.2 — codeword annihilation and arbitrary-error rank bound
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open Filter
/-- Lemma 2.2, with the standing sufficiently-large-n convention of §2. -/
theorem codeword_annihilation (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (g : Geometry (dimension ε) n)
      (s : Forms g.F (dimension ε) (arity ε))
      (h : Hashes g.F (arity ε) (buckets ε n)) (x : Word n),
      testMatrix g ((combined g s h).mulVec x) = 0 ∧
      ∀ e : Word (rowCount (dimension ε) n),
        (testMatrix g ((combined g s h).mulVec x + e)).rank ≤ weight e := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and use the construction and rank matrix from equations (1)–(5). For all sufficiently large $n$, every sampled matrix $G$ and every codeword $c$ in its binary column image satisfy
$$\mathcal M(c)=0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}_{F_q}\mathcal M(c+e)\le|\operatorname{supp}(e)|\quad\text{for every binary }e.$$
Both conclusions hold for all coefficient vectors and hash functions, including every nonexpanding output. Errors may depend on $c$ and on $G$.

This is the algebraic guarantee underlying the arbitrary-error test. Codewords are written as $Gx$ for arbitrary binary $x$, which ranges over the complete column image.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: one-based vectors, fixed finite fields and sufficiently large input size → zero-based finite indices, public field/row equivalences, and an eventual assertion before all outputs; reason: these are the same objects and the standing sufficiently-large-n convention; no sampler output is excluded
- encoding: c ranges over the binary column image of G → c is Gx for every binary message x; reason: a generator column image consists exactly of these products, without any rank condition
